analyst.summary: Eicher Motors had a record FY26 - Royal Enfield sold 1.22 million motorcycles, VECV's truck volumes rose 15%, and consolidated profit grew 17% - and June 2026's monthly numbers beat Street estimates on both the motorcycle and truck side. But the September-2025 GST change that made sub-350cc bikes cheaper and 450cc-plus bikes more expensive is quietly working against the higher-margin upgrade cycle: Himalayan 450 and Super Meteor 650 volumes actually fell in FY26, even as overall company volumes rose on cheaper entry-level bikes. Competition from Honda, the Bajaj-Triumph-KTM-Husqvarna stable, Harley-Davidson and Jawa-Yezdi-BSA keeps widening, even if Royal Enfield's overall lead is still large. At close to 37 times trailing earnings - a premium to other listed two-wheeler makers - the stock already prices in continued strong growth, and the new electric Flying Flea motorcycle is a long-term option, not yet a profit contributor. We rate this Hold: a well-run, dominant franchise, priced for a smoother growth path than its most profitable segment is currently delivering.
